newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-FRITZ STROBL FASTEST IN VAL GARDENA.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-FRITZ STROBL FASTEST IN VAL GARDENA.

text.p: Austrian Fritz Strobl, winner of the first men's World Cup Alpine skiing downhill of the season in France last weekend, again set the pace on Wednesday in opening training in Val Gardena.
The 24-year-old police cadet from the southern province of Carinthia was the only racer on the challenging Saslong piste to complete the 3.4-km run in under two minutes.
Strobl clocked a time of one minute 59.82 seconds, 0.86 of a second faster than Kristian Ghedina of Italy and unrelated Austrian Josef Strobl, who tied in second place.
Strobl, largely overshadowed by the rest of the Austrian squad until his win in Val d'Isere on Sunday, appeared nonchalant about his time afterwards.
"I've won Val d'Isere. The only pressure that I have now is in my ski boots," said the Austrian, who crashed out in Val Gardena last year during a Europa Cup event.

The Austrians, who wear the new nickname of "The Eagle Knights" on their snowjackets, dominated the run with four men in the top seven but they could not repeat the whitewash of opening training at Val d'Isere when they had the top six.
They went on to fill the four top places at Val d'Isere, ahead of Ghedina and Frenchman Luc Alphand.

World Cup downhill champion Alphand cleared the air with Patrick Ortlieb, world champion and winner here for the last two years, after saying in Val D'Isere that he did not like the way the big Austrian skier sometimes behaves.
His comments were blown up by the Austrian media and Alphand made clear that there had been a misunderstanding.
"We have no problems between us on a personal level," said the Frenchman, who was equal sixth fastest with Austrian Andreas Schifferer in 2:01.03. Ortlieb was 18th fastest in 2:02.30.
"We are rivals on the pistes and I get a lot of pleasure out of beating him just as he does in beating me.
"That's as far as it goes," he said.
Ghedina said the Saslong piste, with its famous "Camel humps" halfway down and bumpy Ciaslat curve, was hard and icy for most of its length but "pretty easy for us to ski".
"It's a bit icy in places but it's not hard to hold the line, it hasn't been iced," he said at the finish.
Val Gardena is hosting two World Cup downhills, one on Friday and another on Saturday, making up for a race postponed from Whistler, Canada, due to heavy snowfall.
Olympic champion Tommy Moe, never higher than 12th in Val Gardena, was eighth fastest in two minutes 01.39 seconds, an impressive run after recent poor form and injuries.
"There was one turn I had a mistake on in the Ciaslat but it was a pretty good run," the American said. "I like this kind of piste, with big turns and hard snow.
"I know I can ski as fast as Alphand and Ortlieb. I just have to find it mentally. A top 15 position would be nice, a top 10 would be great," the Alaskan skier added.
